### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**30** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d6589d569260a21a3117c417fad74f55158fd06`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d6589d569260a21a3117c417fad74f55158fd06` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1ac50d0a25eb56888e8ce42ef77c6bde9f66efbc` — the merge of head `7557e7bc00848d36b5acb442eb4b9023220134f0` into base `0d6589d569260a21a3117c417fad74f55158fd06`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1ac50d0a25eb56888e8ce42ef77c6bde9f66efbc && git checkout 1ac50d0a25eb56888e8ce42ef77c6bde9f66efbc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d6589d569260a21a3117c417fad74f55158fd06 7557e7bc00848d36b5acb442eb4b9023220134f0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d6589d569260a21a3117c417fad74f55158fd06 && git merge --no-ff 7557e7bc00848d36b5acb442eb4b9023220134f0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d6589d569260a21a3117c417fad74f55158fd06
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0d6589d569260a21a3117c417fad74f55158fd06` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7557e7bc00848d36b5acb442eb4b9023220134f0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts

Read: card #36626 and its four comments (triage, claim 7118541509, the claim correction, the os-dev-report), the PR body, the net diff `844218f5..7557e7bc` (21 files), and the check-runs on the head. Code read outside the diff, not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.ts` (`CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_KEYS`, `extensionArrangementKeys`), `packages/objectql/src/registry-custom-arrangement.ts` (the fold), `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/packageCustomizations-io.ts` (the first strict consumer).

### ① Derived judgments

- `GetPackageCustomizationsResponseSchema` gains a required `arrangements` array of strict `{ object, key }` entries and a required `counts.arrangements`. Right: every list of this answer is required and has a count, and the `contributions` widening (changeset 8196881) set that precedent with the same shape of change.
- `key` is `z.enum(CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_KEYS)`, imported from `../data/field-customization`, not a second literal list. Right: the spec test pins `key.options` to the frozen list, so a fourth key added there widens this answer in the same commit.
- The entry is strict and carries no content. Right against the docblock's ADR-0146 D2/D6 line (served rows only, no diff against the base): a content-bearing entry is refused `unrecognized_keys`, pinned in the spec test.
- The accept-set moves both ways for a strict parser: the new schema refuses an answer without the two members, and the schema of the previous version refuses the new answer. Right as declared: the changeset says so, the one in-repo strict consumer (`packageCustomizations-io.ts`) ships from the same tree, and its ten fixtures moved in this diff.
- `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` gains `api/GetPackageCustomizationsResponse:arrangements`, one key. Right, and it is what makes `Metadata-protocol: added` the true value.
- No existing member changes shape; `extensions` and `counts.extensions` are untouched by an arrangement (pinned: the real-protocol case expects `extensions` empty).

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/runtime` matches what the diff publishes: one added response member with its count, and a producer that starts serving it. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds: a declared capability is added and none is taken away; the strict-parse consequence for an older schema is stated in the changeset, as the `contributions` precedent stated it. `Metadata-protocol: added` holds against the tree (the moved authorable-surface shard); the claim's `none` was corrected on the card at 02:17Z. `Check Changeset` is success on its latest run (02:20:38Z); the 02:12Z failure is superseded.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, `actionLayout` listed beside the two keys the card names: accepted. The card's ask is the arrangement keys of an extension; iterating the frozen list is the one rule, and leaving the third key out would need a second hand-written list that the fold and the doors do not read.
- Deviation, file surface widened (10 ui fixtures, the mount test, the strictness-ledger count, `metadata-api.mdx`): accepted as riders of a strict required member; none is a second change.
- Deviation, `Metadata-protocol` corrected to `added` and the changeset to `minor`: correct, see ②.
- Deviation, seat stamp line placed after the five fixed lines of the PR body: no contract effect; `PR-body guards` is success.
- Deviation, the dedupe across two pairs is unpinned by a test: accepted. The code path is four lines over a `Set` keyed on object and key, and it agrees with the fold, which serves one writer per key and names the other.
- Out-of-scope notes (the Studio landing's "n customized" sum; `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md:129` naming three of the lists): both stay true on this head. Neither is owed here.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The hunk adds no query, no id materialisation and no join; it reads the in-memory registry contributors inside the loop that already feeds `extensions`.
- Check-runs on the head: every current run is success or skipped, `Test Core`, `Test UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` included.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts`. Against ADR-0146 D10 as `field-customization.ts` states it, and against ruling 6566915346 letter E as the docblock quotes it: the entry shape is per kind, strict, and nothing is joined by name; an arrangement is one declaration of the whole object, so its own list and not an `extensions` member is the right place. Against the first consumer: the console reader parses through this schema and adds only `counts.overrides` and `counts.extensions`, so the new member changes no number it shows. Tried to break it: a `fields` key is refused at `arrangements[0].key`, a content-bearing entry is refused, both members are required. Held.

`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, `readPackageCustomizations`, sentence by sentence against the schema's description:
- "an object the base owns": the loop's existing `getObjectOwner(name)?.packageId !== baseId` guard covers the new hunk. Pinned (`other_note` not listed).
- "the paired package writes": `contributor.packageId !== pairId || ownership !== 'extend'` is the existing guard. Pinned (the dependent's `fieldGroups` not listed).
- "carries a value under (an empty list included)": `extensionArrangementKeys`, the reading the fold uses (`registry-custom-arrangement.ts:158`). Pinned with `relatedLists: []`.
- "whichever of the base's pairs writes it", one entry per object and key: the `Set` dedupe over `pairsOf(baseId, …)`, the same pair lookup the fold's context names.
- "Ordered by object, then key in the order …": the sort by `localeCompare`, then `CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_KEYS.indexOf`. Pinned by the four-entry case.
- "`arrangements.length`": derived in the same answer.
- Agreement with the served object is pinned through the real protocol: draft save, publish, then `_relatedListsArrangement.packageId` is the pair and the base's own declaration is unchanged, which is the card's acceptance.

`packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts`: the note's added clause says what the schema and the producer say. Agrees.

Nits, no effect on correctness or the contract:
- N1 (nit): the list is what the pair's extension writes, not what the fold serves. The fold withholds a disabled package's contribution and skips a key whose value is not a list or an object, while this read lists both. The description says "writes", so the code agrees with it, and `extensions` reads the same contributors the same way on `main`. `contributions` states its disabled rule in its description; `arrangements` does not. A follow-up card could add the sentence.
- N2 (nit): the docblock says the arrangement itself is "the pair's stored `object_extension` item", and the entry names no package. Where the App's pair and an older per-package pair both write one key, the entry does not say which pair's item is served. The fold serves the App's pair; a reader who needs the content can ask the served object. Same follow-up, if any.

### Read
- `l1-face.mjs --pr 36818` at this head: 12 of 13 items ok. Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #36626`, no other card bound, changesets for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/runtime` (both minor). `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` match the claim as corrected. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check success.
- The one flag, `all-checks` (1 failed, Check Changeset), counts a superseded run. With `filter=all`, Check Changeset has two runs on this head: 138164235647 failure (02:12Z) and 138167701983 success (02:20Z, after the body fix). The latest run per name is green: 62 success / 11 expected skip / 0 failed.
- Not governed (`check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 36818`: 0 of 21 paths hit the register; +310/−31).
- Changeset, `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx` and the regenerated `content/docs/references/api/package-lifecycle.mdx` read sentence by sentence against the producer (`readPackageCustomizations`: same pair loop as `extensions`, `extensionArrangementKeys(body)`, deduped per object and key, sorted by object then `CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_KEYS` order). True at this head. No new UI string.
- Card acceptance (HotCRM 「线索」 tab reorder/hide → the read lists it, base unchanged): met by a real-protocol test that uses the console writer's draft-save-then-publish into the pair, not by a live HotCRM run. The body declares this, and I accept it as the evidence.
- `actionLayout` comes along as a declared deviation: one rule over the frozen `CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_KEYS`. Accepted: the card names `relatedLists` and `fieldGroups`, and the third key costs no second reading.

### Findings

- **M1 (claim surface, paper).** Claim 7118541509's surface names the producer's one test (`domains/packages-customizations.test.ts`) plus the spec tests, generated artefacts, docs, the client type and a changeset. The diff also edits `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.package-customizations-mount.test.ts` and ten existing `ui/packages/app-shell` tests (fixtures given the new member). The body names them as riders, but the claim was not amended, and correction 7119967656 changes only the `Metadata-protocol:` line. Fix: the seat posts a claim amendment naming those eleven test files. No head move.
- **S1 (`Skills-docs:` value not true as written).** The line reads `updated here — content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx …` and says `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md:129` "stays true". That skill line is the same sentence this PR rewrites in `metadata-api.mdx`: "`GET /packages/hotcrm/customizations` lists its overrides, extensions and switched-off items". After this PR it leaves out the fifth list, the one a tab arrangement now shows up in, while the docs copy of the sentence is corrected. `updated here` names a `content/docs` page, not the skill. For kind `added`, the skill text that teaches this read is owed, so the honest value is `follow-up owed — #N`, with a `domain:skills` card the seat files (`skills/**` would make this PR Tier H). Fix: patch the PR body's `Skills-docs:` line to that value once the card exists. No head move.

- N1. Studio's landing count does not move for an arrangement. `customizationMarks.ts:98` counts `overrides + extensions`, so a base whose only customization is a tab arrangement still reads as not customized there, even though this read now lists it. Outside the card, which asks for the read. User effect, so it goes to the seat as a possible follow-up.
- N2 (disclosed). The dedupe across two pairs (an App's pair and a per-package pair writing one key on one object) is unpinned. One `{ object, key }` entry is the only meaningful reading, and the `Set` makes it so by construction. No effect.
- N3. A client parsing through an older `@objectstack/spec` refuses the new member. The changeset says so. This is the widening's own cost, judged in the L2 record.

Delta read owed: M1 and S1 are paper (claim amendment, PR-body line), so the head need not move. I re-read the claim and body on this head once both are posted.
